changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For membership businesses, lead with churn, not with retries. Suggested line: 'Some of your churn is members who never meant to leave. Their card failed. We'll show you which of your own failed renewals are recoverable.' Back the claim with an analysis of the prospect's own failed-renewal export, not an average.
changes.why: The buyer saw the problem as lost members ('members who never meant to leave'), and recovery only moved the deal once it was shown on their own file ('Their file, not our average.'), after which it signed four days later.

changes.change: Add a finance-ready proof step for the controller or whoever holds the paper: a spreadsheet scoring the prospect's own failed renewals as recoverable or not, which they can take away. Run it before the contract reaches finance, not after it stalls. Have a plain answer ready on contract term and exit cost.
changes.why: The paper sat with the silent controller for two weeks. It moved only when he 'asked for the spreadsheet' from the data session, and he had asked about termination fees twice.

changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For membership studio buyers, stop using the 'unified commerce' label and the 'one platform' claim for in-store. Say instead that in-store payments at the front desk run through a partner integration with their studio software, offered as a phase two. Show it live in their own setup before claiming more.
changes.why: 'Unified commerce' meant only 'is that the readers?' to the champion, and we could not show the reader working live inside their studio software. That left the front desk with the incumbent, with phase two dependent on 'the partner piece'.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For membership businesses with studios in the US and Canada, don't open with the global slide. Open with their churn and recoverable failed renewals (see the M10 change).
changes.why: The rep 'opened with the global slide' to a business with studios in the US and a handful in Canada, and it did not land. What they cared about was the churn number they report to the board.
